newsitem.title: MEXICO: 14 Mexicans, 30,000 political smear videos seized.
newsitem.headline: 14 Mexicans, 30,000 political smear videos seized.

text.p: Police arrested 14 Mexicans on Thursday, accusing them of issuing a video smearing leftist leader Cuauhtemoc Cardenas and his party as violent radicals before major Mexico City elections on July 6.

The suspects were seized overnight during a police raid on a clandestine video duplicating shop in the upscale Condesa neighbourhood. Authorities said 30,000 of the videos were stored there, ready to be distributed.
The video, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, shows Cardenas, an opposition candidate for mayor of Mexico City, promising a peaceful campaign and rejecting violence.
It then cuts to images of radicals burning buses, hurling Molotov cocktails and stoning police. Some of the protesters wave banners of Cardenas' Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
PRD officials accused the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) of organising the video to hurt Cardenas, who is well ahead in the first race for Mexico City mayor in modern history.

"We caught them red-handed," Jesus Ortega, secretary general of the PRD, told Mexico City's Radio Red. "This is part of the smear campaign against our party and against Cuauhtemoc Cardenas in particular."
Alfredo del Mazo, the PRI candidate running a distant second in the Mexico City race, denied knowing anything about the tapes and called for an investigation.
"Anything that in any way leads to a dirty war is inconvenient," he said. "Nothing like this should happen."
Mexican elections have long been plagued by charges of dirty tricks, which the opposition says have helped the PRI maintain its 68-year grip on power.
The government has pledged that the elections, which include a federal vote to renew the 500-seat Chamber of Deputies, will be the cleanest ever.
Mexican Attorney General Jorge Madrazo said the detainees could face a series of charges, but it was not clear whether any electoral laws had been broken.
The video is signed by two unknown groups: Business Action and the National Council of Popular Organisations.
Besides the anti-PRD video, the house where it was duplicated contained pornographic material, police said.
